narrative.executive_summary: This compliance evidence report (ID: compliance-20260825T033941Z) presents the results of automated control evaluation conducted against four regulatory and best-practice frameworks: CIS Controls v8, ISO 27001, NIST CSF 2.0, and PCI DSS 4.0. All four evaluated controls passed, yielding an overall score of 100% (4 of 4 controls). The evidence confirms that key AWS infrastructure components supporting web application protection, threat correlation, incident response, and executive security reporting are active and present as of the evaluation timestamp. This report provides control evidence only and does not constitute a formal certification or regulatory compliance attestation.
narrative.overall_assessment: The automated evaluation returned a PASS status across all four controls and all four frameworks assessed. Evidence confirms the existence and active status of three DynamoDB tables supporting WAF event logging, threat correlation findings, and security incident tracking, as well as an S3 prefix containing executive security reports. No control failures or items requiring review were identified in this evaluation run. The evidence supports that foundational security infrastructure is in place; however, the presence of active resources does not by itself confirm continuous or effective operation of the underlying security processes.
strengths: CTRL-001 (AWS WAF Protection): The DynamoDB table 'armageddon-summer-2026-dev-waf-events' is confirmed ACTIVE, indicating that infrastructure for capturing and storing WAF events is in place, supporting network security monitoring aligned with NIST CSF 2.0 PR.PS-1, CIS Controls v8 13.1, PCI DSS 4.0 6.4, and ISO 27001 A.8.20.

CTRL-002 (Threat Correlation): The DynamoDB table 'armageddon-summer-2026-dev-waf-correlation-findings' is confirmed ACTIVE, indicating that a dedicated store for correlated security findings exists, supporting detection capabilities aligned with NIST CSF 2.0 DE.AE-03 and CIS Controls v8 13.7.

CTRL-003 (Incident Response): The DynamoDB table 'armageddon-summer-2026-dev-security-incidents' is confirmed ACTIVE, indicating that infrastructure for recording and tracking security incidents is in place, supporting incident response processes aligned with NIST CSF 2.0 RS.MA-01 and CIS Controls v8 17.3.

CTRL-004 (Executive Security Reporting): The S3 prefix 's3://armageddon-summer-2026-dev-armageddon-executive-reports/reports' is confirmed to contain report evidence, indicating that a governance reporting mechanism is operational and supports security visibility for leadership, aligned with NIST CSF 2.0 GV.OV-01.
Full framework coverage achieved: All four frameworks (CIS Controls v8, ISO 27001, NIST CSF 2.0, PCI DSS 4.0) returned a 100% pass score in this evaluation run.
recommended_actions: Validate that the WAF events DynamoDB table (CTRL-001) is actively receiving and retaining event data, not merely that the table exists, to confirm end-to-end WAF protection is functioning.

Confirm that the threat correlation findings table (CTRL-002) contains current, populated findings to demonstrate that the detection and correlation pipeline is producing actionable output, not only that the storage resource is present.

Verify that the security incidents table (CTRL-003) reflects an active incident response workflow, including evidence of incident lifecycle management, to substantiate process operation beyond infrastructure existence.
Review the contents of the executive reporting S3 prefix (CTRL-004) to confirm that reports are current, complete, and being consumed by leadership, supporting meaningful governance oversight.
Establish a recurring evaluation cadence to ensure control evidence remains current and reflects ongoing operational status rather than point-in-time resource existence.
Consider expanding evidence collection to include data-plane metrics (e.g., record counts, last-write timestamps, report generation dates) to strengthen the evidentiary basis for future audits.
evidence_limitations: All control evidence is based solely on the existence and ACTIVE status of AWS resources (DynamoDB tables and an S3 prefix). The evaluation does not confirm that these resources contain data, are receiving current inputs, or are being actively used by security processes.

The evidence does not demonstrate continuous operation of any control. A resource being ACTIVE at the time of evaluation does not prove it was operational at all prior points in the assessment period.

No data-plane evidence (e.g., record counts, item timestamps, WAF rule configurations, report file dates) was included in this evaluation. The absence of such evidence limits conclusions about the effectiveness or completeness of each control.
No ownership, process, or personnel information was provided. It is not possible to confirm accountability or procedural adherence from the available evidence.
This report covers four controls only. The scope does not represent a comprehensive assessment of the organization's security posture or all controls required by the referenced frameworks.
This report provides control evidence as evaluated by automated tooling and does not constitute a legal, regulatory, or certification compliance determination for any of the referenced frameworks.
narrative.auditor_note: All statuses and scores in this report are reproduced exactly as produced by the automated Python evaluation engine and have not been altered, recalculated, or overridden. The evidence confirms resource existence and active status for four AWS infrastructure components as of report ID compliance-20260825T033941Z. Auditors should note that resource existence alone is not equivalent to demonstrated control effectiveness; supplementary data-plane evidence, process documentation, and operational records should be requested to support a complete audit conclusion.
